reason: Verified by driving master.html?v=approach at 390/768/1440 and by reading render-b.js and b.css. Three of the four sub-claims hold and none is covered by the gates. (1) The past block is an unnamed assertion on the guest surface: b.css:269 sets [data-past="folded"] .b-behindRow{display:none} and the approach room defaults past="folded" (render-core.js:189), so all three .b-behindRow entries -- 'Fri 2 Jan We said yes', 'Sat 18 Apr The Orchard reserved', 'No date City hotel shortlist' -- compute display:none, leaving only 'Behind you / 2 done, the last of them 18 April. One thing is not going ahead.' phone and desk have ZERO focusable elements in total, so there is no control to open it; the b.css comment above the block ('opens if anyone wants it') describes a console knob, not a page. A cancellation announced with no name, no date and no way to reach it is the one sentence on a wedding page that plants doubt and cannot resolve it. (2) Reading order does swap: .b-behind resolves after .b-measure in the DOM at state=phone and before it at desk, print and owner-flight, which also contradicts the source's own stated intent in b.css ('It sits under the measure'). (3) Heading spine: the only heading in the accessibility tree on phone, desk, print AND owner-flight is h2 'Behind you'. There is no h1 anywhere on the guest surfaces -- the couple's name is p.b-who, the day is p.b-when, 'days away' is p.b-measureHead -- so the single landmark a screen-reader user can jump to is the least important region on the page. Two corrections to the finding, neither fatal: 'Nothing is planned for the next 16 days.' is NOT the loudest sentence on the screen (15px at 62% ink, against a 96/148px numeral and a 20/30px date); it is the only prose sentence under the accent rule, which is the real point. And 'Behind you' is second person but not owner-only language -- that strand is the weakest and is not what makes this real. The fix as written is refused in two places and sharpened below: deleting the gap note re-opens the ~550px of unexplained empty rail it exists to explain and restates the lead row that sits directly beneath it, and deleting 'Behind you' from the guest surfaces removes the only evidence the plan has a history without fixing the actual defect, which is that the sentence names nothing.
sharpenedFix: Four changes, all in render-b.js and b.css, no new colour, weight or family. (a) Keep the gap note and its job -- explaining the void -- but state it as distance, not absence: 'The next thing is 16 days away.' derived from the same F.daysTo(ahead()[0].date). Do not restate the lead item's title 550px above itself. (b) Do not cut behindBlock from the guest surfaces. Make the named rows visible there instead: the listed rendering already exists (b.css:251-267, data-past="listed", cancelled title already struck), so drop the folded default for this block, show its three rows, add the vocabulary label 'Not going ahead' beside the struck title (F.stateLabel.cancelled, already in fixture.js), and rewrite .b-behindNote to drop the unnamed cancellation now that the item is on the page -- 'Two things are settled.' with the rows carrying the rest. If the block must stay foldable, give it a real disclosure button with aria-expanded rather than a console attribute. (c) Fix the order in states.desk, states.print and the two owner states: leave horizon alone in .b-stick and move behindBlock into the right column after measure(), so the past follows the measure at every width, as b.css already claims it does. (d) Do not add new h1 copy. Promote the existing elements: render .b-who inside the horizon as h1 (declaring font-weight:400 the way .b-behindLabel already does, so the two-weight lock holds and nothing moves visually), promote .b-measureHead to h2, keep .b-behindLabel as the h2 after it. That gives phone, desk, print and owner one h1 and two h2s with zero visual change and no new strings.
